title: [oneTBB backend] macOS < 10.13 with libc++ need `-fno-aligned-allocation`
description:
@eddelbuettel Could we fix this? The issue arises only with OneTBB backend and Clang with `libc++` on < 10.13 (that is why we did not face it earlier: legacy TBB was used until recently).

We could fix it for dependents of `RcppParallel` like this:
https://github.com/macports/macports-ports/pull/24545/commits/627f0ddd37c8a343493f13ecab580665d294a97c

But considering a number of affected ports, it is somewhat suboptimal solution.

(To be explicit, this should not be used with gcc and `libstdc++` on any macOS versions, including < 10.13. Everything works fine there, and also the flag is Clang-specific.)

title: Error in lazy loading for reverse dependencies of qs2
description:
I get the following error for my Bioconductor packages which import or suggest qs2 (CSOA, GSABenchmark, hammers, scLang):

> Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
> unable to load shared object '/home/biocbuild/bbs-3.24-bioc/R/site-library/qs2/libs/qs2.so':
> /home/biocbuild/bbs-3.24-bioc/R/site-library/qs2/libs/qs2.so: undefined symbol: _ZTIN3tbb4taskE
> Calls: ... asNamespace -> loadNamespace -> library.dynam -> dyn.load
> Execution halted
> ERROR: lazy loading failed for package ‘CSOA’

https://www.bioconductor.org/checkResults/3.24/bioc-LATEST/CSOA/nebbiolo2-install.html

Checking results on Bioconductor (https://www.bioconductor.org/checkResults/3.24/bioc-LATEST/), I found that other reverse dependencies of qs2 (ChromSCape, cTRAP, gDRimport, gDRutils, etc.) have the same issue.

I [asked](https://github.com/qsbase/qs2/issues/30) about this error in the qs2 repository and @traversc told me the following:

> Thanks for the report. The issue is not qs2 (you can see it's all green on the CRAN page), its due to a RcppParallel update which changed ABI. The only thing you need to do is reinstall qs2 from source

The error is not on my side (presumably because my version of RcppParallel is older than the mentioned update), it's on the Bioconductor side. Could you please investigate and fix this?

title: RcppParallel 6.1.1: `tbbLibraryPath()` broken on Windows - looks in build-time RTools not runtime
description:
The use of `RcppParallel::tbbLibraryPath("tbb")` on Windows returns nothing when called from the CRAN pre-built binary, and `tbbRoot()` returns a filepath on a `D:/` drive:

``` r
utils::packageVersion("RcppParallel")
#> [1] '6.1.1'
RcppParallel::tbbLibraryPath("tbb")
RcppParallel:::tbbRoot()
#> [1] "D:/rtools45/x86_64-w64-mingw32.static.posix/lib"
```

All works as expected when `RcppParallel` is built from source:

``` r
install.packages("RcppParallel", type = "source")
#> Installing package into 'C:/Users/andrew/AppData/Local/R/win-library/4.6'
#> (as 'lib' is unspecified)
RcppParallel::tbbLibraryPath("tbb")
#> [1] "C:/rtools45/x86_64-w64-mingw32.static.posix/lib/libtbb12.a"
RcppParallel:::tbbRoot()
#> [1] "C:/rtools45/x86_64-w64-mingw32.static.posix/lib"
```

This appears to be due to `RcppParallel` looking in the dir specified by the internal [`TBB_LIB` variable set by the configure run](https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/39afcb3fcf5ca83241901eef18dac8ed0700f7ef/R/tbb.R#L121) at package build time, rather than the location at runtime

title: RcppParallel.h disables TBB on Alpine Linux
description:
[Documentation](https://rcppcore.github.io/RcppParallel/tbb.html#portability) says packages should call tbb only `#if RCPP_PARALLEL_USE_TBB`, which is false on Alpine Linux due to
<https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/69d50f65fa6cfc8163cccf09c6a500e55f1e24a7/inst/include/RcppParallel.h#L13-L17>
I was able to successfully install RcppParallel using the system TBB (via `--configure-vars='TBB_LIB=/usr/lib TBB_INC=/usr/include'`), but the above means packages LinkingTo RcppParallel won't usually use TBB anyway.

Furthermore, several packages don't seem to use TBB conditionally, at least

- ~~CaseBasedReasoning~~
- ~~DER~~
- FLSSS
- ~~GenomeAdmixR~~
- RcppMeCab
- ~~Scalelink~~
- bgms
- evesim
- ~~junctions~~
- ~~secsse~~

fail to compile on Alpine Linux with errors such as "error: 'tbb' does not name a type" or "error: 'tbb' has not been declared" (see the corresponding outputs at <https://github.com/bastistician/Rcheck/tree/results/musl/issues>).

Is there something RcppParallel[.h] could do better with regard to its default setting so TBB is used by packages on Alpine Linux if RcppParallel was installed with the system TBB?

title: Feature request: add a check if the process has been forked for TBB safety
Unexpected triggering of multithreading
description:
When submitting R packages for verification to CRAN, we receive (on multiple packages), the following results:

```
* checking tests ... [114s/21s] NOTE
  Running ‘testthat.R’ [114s/21s]
Running R code in ‘testthat.R’ had CPU time 5.6 times elapsed time
* checking for unstated dependencies in vignettes ... OK
* checking package vignettes ... OK
* checking re-building of vignette outputs ... [165s/26s] NOTE
Re-building vignettes had CPU time 6.4 times elapsed time
```

Suggesting that the code was executed in a multi-threaded fashion. However, in all our code-calls, we set the number of threads to 1. We have double checked this, and now also return the number of threads after executing back to 1. To no avail.

Our packages use tbb in Rcpp, and we set the number of threads on the R side through:

```
RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(num_threads)
```
And collect the number of threads on the Rcpp side through:
```
auto* nt_env = std::getenv("RCPP_PARALLEL_NUM_THREADS");
auto num_threads = (nullptr == nt_env)
                                ? tbb::task_arena::automatic
                                : static_cast<size_t>(std::atoi(nt_env));
auto global_control =  tbb::global_control(tbb::global_control::max_allowed_parallelism, 
                                                                        num_threads);
```

Parallelization inside the Rcpp code is then invoked through `tbb::parallel_for` .

It seems however that at the check at CRAN (Debian, Clang 20), the global control doesn't work, and multiple threads are still created.

I can not replicate this issue on macos (my machine) or on rhub (no multi threading) or GHA (no multi threading).

Is this a known issue // are we setting something up incorrectly somewhere?

I am facing a few errors installing and using RcppParallel along with oneTBB on MacOS Big Sur. 

### Installation of oneTBB
1. I have compiled and installed oneTBB to the directory `oneTBB_install` under home directory. I have then exported the variables `TBB`, `TBB_INC` and `TBB_LIB` as `<$HOME>/oneTBB_install`, `<$HOME>/oneTBB_install/include` and `<$HOME>/oneTBB_install/lib` respectively. 
2. I have also defined these variables in ~/.R/Makevars

1. when I attempt to install RcppParallel using , the installation process mentions that 
(a) tbb is being built from "bundled" sources, and

title: RcppParallelLibs() example and CRAN
description:
Hi there

The example in the documentation for added RcppParallel to R packages is the following:

https://rcppcore.github.io/RcppParallel/#r_packages

**src\Makevars**
```
PKG_LIBS += $(shell ${R_HOME}/bin/Rscript -e "RcppParallel::RcppParallelLibs()")
```

**src\Makevars.win**

```
PKG_CXXFLAGS += -DRCPP_PARALLEL_USE_TBB=1

PKG_LIBS += $(shell "${R_HOME}/bin${R_ARCH_BIN}/Rscript.exe" \
              -e "RcppParallel::RcppParallelLibs()")

```


Question: is this CRAN compatible? The CRAN checks have been cracking down on `+=` and `${shell .. }` recently. GNU shell functions are not accepted. 

https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Writing-portable-packages

If the above is not CRAN-acceptable, would it be possible to provide new best standards to the community?

According to the manual:

> 
> The use of ${shell ...} can be avoided by using backticks, e.g.
> 
> PKG_CPPFLAGS = `gsl-config --cflags`
> which works in all versions of make known[74](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#FOOT74) to be used with R.
>

Thoughts?

Thanks for the help

title: RcppParallel.h introduces conflicting macro variables on Mac
description:
On Mac, RcppParallel.h introduces TRUE and FALSE macro variables brought in from system headers (mach/boolean.h) that conflict with TRUE and FALSE definitions from R headers. 

If RcppParallel.h is added to <package_name>_types.h, it then [breaks RcppExports.cpp](https://github.com/traversc/mactest/actions/runs/8024331210/job/21922675174#step:7:97).

A simple fix could be to undef TRUE and FALSE in RcppParallel.h. Reproducible example: https://github.com/traversc/mactest/blob/main/src/mactest_types.h#L9

Alternatively, TRUE and FALSE macros could be re-assigned to something else like R_TRUE and R_FALSE in RcppExports.cpp

title: tbb.h deprecated features
description:
Packages compiling against RcppParallel show:

```
In file included from /usr/local/lib/R/library/RcppParallel/include/RcppParallel/TBB.h:10,
                 from /usr/local/lib/R/library/RcppParallel/include/RcppParallel.h:21,
                 from fittingFunctions.cpp:6:
/usr/include/tbb/tbb.h:21:154: note: '#pragma message: TBB Warning: tbb.h contains deprecated functionality. For details, please see Deprecated Features appendix in the TBB reference manual.'
   21 | #pragma message("TBB Warning: tbb.h contains deprecated functionality. For details, please see Deprecated Features appendix in the TBB reference manual.")
      |                                                                                                                                                          ^
```

`tbb/tbb.h` is included [here](https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/9dcfa620b2b9a95023b490e439f11e1380f8df78/inst/include/RcppParallel/TBB.h#L10). We should think about moving away from that header.

title: `CXX_STD = CXX11` causes CRAN note on devel
description:
`CXX_STD = CXX11` causes a CRAN note. The current CRAN default is C++17 and it doesn't like you to specify an older version.
The easy fix is to change the docs 11 -> 17 but that too will probably be too old someday. Perhaps the docs could just say that at least C++11 is required for RcppParallel to work but not do anything in Makevars?
Up to you how to tackle this, just wanted to make sure you were aware.

title: CRAN asking for C++17
description: My package [lamW](https://cran.r-project.org/package=lamW) depends on RcppParallel. Its [results tab](https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_lamW.html) is now showing a note "Specified C++11: please update to current default of C++17". Is addressing this as simple as updatinge Makevars and Makevars.win to read `CXX_STD = CXX17` or will that create issues? Thank you

title: Cannot load: undefined symbol tbb::task::note_affinity
description:
Are we sure that nothing is required on Linux?

https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/0da9610af0fcfe3154bff8c0e38c9ad22fc9fb62/R/tbb.R#L92-L93

I cannot load the `markovchain` package (cc @spedygiorgio), which links against `RcppParallel`, with the following error:

```
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘markovchain’ in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...):
 unable to load shared object '/usr/local/lib/R/library/markovchain/libs/markovchain.so':
  /usr/local/lib/R/library/markovchain/libs/markovchain.so: undefined symbol: _ZN3tbb4task13note_affinityEt
```

So somehow this TBB symbol ends up in the `markovchain` library. Manually adding `-ltbb` to the linking phase solves the issue for me, but currently `RcppParallel::RcppParallelLibs()` returns nothing for Linux.

title: support relative compiler paths on Windows
description:
https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/2f71e526bae33ea607f452be7a0dda8c91f19be3/tools/config/configure.R#L88-L100

We should only use `cygpath` if truly required (e.g. the compiler is specified with a path like `/mingw64/gcc` that is specially interpreted by the MinGW shell).

title: License incompatibility with TBB
description: The Intel TBB is licencsed under the Apache 2.0 licence. According to the FOSS, this license is only compatible with GPL-3 while it is not compatible with earlier versions of the GPL. Please refer to [the homepage from the GNU project](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-list.en.html#apache2) for their view on the Apache 2.0. There they explicitly list that the GPL-2 is incompatible with the Apache 2.0 license. Currently, RcppParallel is released under the GPL-2 and an update to GPL-3 should be considered, I think.

title: TBB version requirement?
description:
I don't see any version requirement listed in the DESCRIPTION:

https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/659b32615b36de9f570ae319f56793a28013a3a2/DESCRIPTION#L32

Nor in the reference manual:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RcppParallel/RcppParallel.pdf

But on the `RcppParallel` website:

http://rcppcore.github.io/RcppParallel/

I see:

> Intel TBB (v4.3)

However, I don't see any such version over at the TBB repo:

https://github.com/oneapi-src/oneTBB/releases

The source copy in `src/tbb` seems to be "2018 update 8" which does match an upstream release. The oldest release in the repo is "Intel(R) Threading Building Blocks 4.4" -- is "4.3" supposed to mean "no known version requirement", then?

title: Symlinking instead of copying tbb libs
description: The new `TBB_INC` and `TBB_LIB` variables are great, but I noticed that RcppParallel copies tbb's `.so` files into the package directory. Is this really required? This is a problem for system packaging, because RPM generates a unique ID for each binary (see [this](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Releases/FeatureBuildId)), and thus copying a shared library makes these IDs collide, and the package cannot be installed. Would it be possible to symlink `TBB_LIB` instead?

title: Error installing my package with recent RcppParallel updates
description:
Hi. I am using RcppParallel in my package [phylosmith](https://github.com/schuyler-smith/phylosmith) for implementing openMP. I hadn't had any issues with the installation until recently where i get the error when R tries to load it

```
*** installing help indices

I reinistalled a previous version of RcppParallel and the error doesn't occur. My understanding is this has something to do with TBB libraries, but I don't have enough understanding to know what I didn't include that would cause the updates to throw this error now. I assume it would be something in my [makevars](https://github.com/schuyler-smith/phylosmith/blob/master/src/Makevars) file(s). I tried to update them on my local copy to reflect the documentation [here](https://rcppcore.github.io/RcppParallel/#r_packages), but still the same result. I also tried updating the flags for oneTBB as detailed on the RcppParallel github page README, and that didn't change the results either.

If you have any ideas of where I should be looking to fix my issues, it'd be much appreciated!

title: Optional use of tbbmalloc_proxy (to speedup macOS)?
description:
The RcppParallel provided Intel TBB library is being used in `RStan` for a while now. In benchmarks we found out that specifically on macOS the use of the `tbbmalloc_proxy` library speeds up Stan programs by ~20%. Loading the `tbbmalloc_proxy` library replaces all calls to the system `malloc` to the replacement from the TBB. The upside of doing so is that no source code needs to be changed at all in order to gain from the speed benefits of the TBB provided `malloc`, which is designed to work well will threaded programs ([see here for details](https://www.threadingbuildingblocks.org/tutorial-intel-tbb-scalable-memory-allocator)).

From running benchmarks with Stan programs it turned out that there are clear speedups of ~20% on macOS when using the TBB malloc while other platforms did not really gain in speed. This is why the TBB malloc is only enabled for Stan programs on macOS, but there the speed gains are really nice.

So I wonder if this would be of interest to enable (maybe optionally) loading the `tbbmalloc_proxy` with `RcppParallel`.

If that is an option, I am happy to provide a PR for such an optional feature. If there is anything to consider for such a feature, please let me know.

title: Store version info or MD5 hash of the shared TBB objects
description:
`RcppParallel v5.1.2+` creates symlinks of TBB libraries into the package directory if externally linked (see a1fddba85101886b35123c73054c0d904f747d11 & #161). This can break RcppParallel when the original files are moved, removed, or upgraded to an incompatible version (undefined references).  We need to create a function that stores the version info (e.g., `TBB_INTERFACE_VERSION`), or MD5 hash of the shared TBB objects, at build time and check them at runtime, before loading. If there's a mismatch, we continue with a warning that recommends reinstalling the package to relink to (or build) the TBB libraries.

It's important to ensure the integrity of the shared TBB objects, before loading them. This will also inform the users if the package loading failed due to this issue.

title: Does RMatrix support sparse matrices?
description:
Does the `RMatrix` wrapper for `RcppParallel` "work" for sparse matrices?

In particular, I have a sparse matrix of type `dgCMatrix` from the `Matrix` package of `R`, and I want to do some computations on each column of the matrix in parallel via `RcppParallel`. The computations do not involve matrix operations, so there is no desire to use any matrix functions from e.g. Armadillo or Eigen.

The documentation for `RcppArmadillo` carefully does not mention compatibility with `RcppParallel`. The documentation of `RcppParallel` does not specify if `RMatrix` handles sparse matrices, though it does say "matrices of various types" without further elaboration.

The computations are performed column-wise and are embarrassingly parallel between each column. Is `RMatrix` even necessary in this case? Should a sparse matrix from `R` just be passed as `NumericMatrix`?

title: Grainsize calculation on TinyThreads
description:
https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/39303ec773880111435bc7b735ea47703ad87658/inst/include/RcppParallel/TinyThread.h#L68

I was working fine with TBB in my app on Windows, defining the grainsize, but I got problems when porting to Linux and using TinyThreads. So I looked at the code.

Here I can see that, if I have a vector of size `767`, and I set the grainsize to `64` I get the following:

1. Total threads is `8`
2. So, `767/8` is not exact, and the algorithm chooses to do `767/(8-1) ~= 109`
3. So each chunk will be of size `109`. That is fine for my algorithm that needs a chunk larger than, let's say, `60`.
4. There will be `767 / 109 = 7.0366` jobs. That means one job will be of size `4` that is below my grainsize of `64`. And this will break my algorithm.

So, what about the last chunk to be of size `113` instead of `109` + `4`? This will be in conformity with what is expected from grainsize.

I can write a pull request. For now, I'm just discussing the case.

title: licensing: permission to use GPL2 or later
description:
Hello, RcppParallel is GPL2-only (although some of the tests are GPL2 or later). Does this cause problems for packages that are LinkingTo this project but which are GPL2 or later, or GPL3+? If so, is there a way to get permission to distribute a derivative work as GPL3+?

Context: I stopped using RcppParallel for some packages when TBB was causing CRAN check errors but kept some code from RcppParallel in a header file that allowed me to implement the parallel for code with the C++11 thread support (i.e. no tinythread or TBB). Unfortunately my package is GPL3+ and I have been asked to either relicense my package or get permission to redistribute that code as GPL3+. Now would be a good time to switch back to linking to RcppParallel directly, but I don't think that would solve the licensing problem as I still would have to include a GPLv2-only header file.

title: How to set number of threads multiple times in RcppParallel 5.0.2
description:
Thanks all for a great package. We have been using extensively for some large-scale computation; e.g., for non-negative matrix factorization in our new [fastTopics](https://github.com/pcarbo/fastTopics) package.

The [changes](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RcppParallel/NEWS) introduced in RcppParallel 5.0.2, however, break some important functionality. In particular, we would like to be able to set the number of threads on-the-fly for benchmarking the computations. (Apologies if this issue has already been mentioned in a previous GitHub issue.)

Will this functionality be re-introduced in future versions? If not, do you have a suggested workaround? e.g., by setting an environment variable using `Sys.setenv`?

description:

I'm using the matrix benchmark example as a minimal reproducible case with a larger matrix so I can run `top` and watch for threads. Only one `R` instance runs at 100% CPU. Running the benchmark as it is in the example gives the same time for both serial and parallel implementations.

Interestingly the instance has 64 CPUs but auto-detection is returning 1. I'm setting the number of threads anyway.

**test.R**
```R
library("Rcpp")
library("RcppParallel")
setThreadOptions(numThreads = 64)
sourceCpp("parallel.cpp")
m <- matrix(as.numeric(c(1:100000000)), nrow = 10000, ncol=10000)
parallelMatrixSqrt(m)
```

**parallel.cpp**
```cpp
// [[Rcpp::depends(RcppParallel)]]
#include <Rcpp.h>
#include <RcppParallel.h>
using namespace Rcpp;
using namespace RcppParallel;

struct SquareRoot : public Worker
{
   // source matrix
   const RMatrix<double> input;

   // destination matrix
   RMatrix<double> output;

   // initialize with source and destination
   SquareRoot(const NumericMatrix input, NumericMatrix output)
      : input(input), output(output) {}

   // take the square root of the range of elements requested
   void operator()(std::size_t begin, std::size_t end) {
      std::transform(input.begin() + begin,
                     input.begin() + end,
                     output.begin() + begin,
                     ::sqrt);
   }
};

// [[Rcpp::export]]
NumericMatrix parallelMatrixSqrt(NumericMatrix x) {

  // allocate the output matrix
  NumericMatrix output(x.nrow(), x.ncol());

  // SquareRoot functor (pass input and output matrixes)
  SquareRoot squareRoot(x, output);

  // call parallelFor to do the work
  parallelFor(0, x.length(), squareRoot);

  // return the output matrix
  return output;
}

title: parallelFor interrupt when found a solution
description:
I'm trying to implement an algorithm that tests a condition over many elements in a loop.
When one condition if false, then I return false (like function `all()` basically).

Is there any way to tell the other threads to stop when one has found a condition that is false?

title: Performance of RcppParallel for different numThreads
description:
I am developing a tool in which the RcppParallel is important to increase computational efficiency. However, I found when I set a large numThreads, RcppParallel would not increase efficiency any more. The below is an example from https://gallery.rcpp.org/articles/parallel-vector-sum/, and I set different numThreads. It seems that improvement of RcppParallel is limited and would not increase as the increase of numThreads. My question is 1) Is it expected that RcppParallel can only reduce computation time by 1/2 no matter how many numThreads is used; 2) Is there any other options to fully use multiple CPU cores in Rcpp/RcppArmadillo?  

```r
> RcppParallel::defaultNumThreads()
[1] 24
> RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = 1)
> res <- benchmark(vectorSum(v), parallelVectorSum(v), order="relative", replications = 10)
> res[,1:4]
test replications elapsed relative
1         vectorSum(v)           10   1.352    1.000
2 parallelVectorSum(v)           10   1.378    1.019
> 
> RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = 2)
> res <- benchmark(vectorSum(v), parallelVectorSum(v), order="relative", replications = 10)
> res[,1:4]
test replications elapsed relative
2 parallelVectorSum(v)           10   0.670    1.000
1         vectorSum(v)           10   1.117    1.667
> 
> RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = 4)
> res <- benchmark(vectorSum(v), parallelVectorSum(v), order="relative", replications = 10)
> res[,1:4]
test replications elapsed relative
2 parallelVectorSum(v)           10   0.559    1.000
1         vectorSum(v)           10   1.091    1.952
> 
> RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = 24)
> res <- benchmark(vectorSum(v), parallelVectorSum(v), order="relative", replications = 10)
> res[,1:4]
test replications elapsed relative
2 parallelVectorSum(v)           10   0.552    1.000
1         vectorSum(v)           10   1.086    1.967
```

title: Running without TBB
description:
To avoid the well-known UBSAN issues that can arise on CRAN submission (e.g #36), I was attempting to use RcppParallel with just tinythread++.

I tried setting `-DRCPP_PARALLEL_USE_TBB=0` in my `Makevars` and added some macros after every `#include <RcppParallel.h>` in my source files to confirm that that constant remains both set and equal to 0, but `rhub::check_with_sanitizers()` returns errors of the familiar `../../src/tbbmalloc/backref.cpp:154:21: runtime error: index 1 out of bounds for type 'BackRefBlock *[1]'` kind.

I also removed the linker invocation via `RcppParallel::RcppParallelLibs()` in `Makevars` but that doesn't help.

Is there any way to rid myself of the use of TBB through settings in `Makevars`? I am using the simple `parallelVectorSum` example project that RStudio generates.

title: Multithreading not working - how to diagnose?
description:
Hi - We have been having problems implementing an R package (dada2) that relies on RcppParallel on our HPC (180 cores, 1.25 TB RAM). We're running the latest versions of both R (3.6.2) and dada2 (v.1.14.0) and using PBS Pro to submit jobs. It appears that specific steps in dada2 which utilize multithreading via RcppParallel are failing. We recognize that this is likely a problem specific to our installation (or network architecture?) but could use some advice on how to get this working properly. Relevant discussion over on the dada2 Github page is linked below: 
https://github.com/benjjneb/dada2/issues/926#issuecomment-582472391
@benjjneb @kguay @btupper
Thanks,
Pete

description: Headers of i.e. [serial/tbb](https://github.com/01org/tbb/tree/tbb_2019/include/serial/tbb) is mentioned [here](https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/blob/master/inst/include/index.html) but not included currently. `tbb::serial::parallel_for` may be helpful for troubeshooting and debugging.

title: build and expose tbb static library
description:
Is it possible make static version (`libtbb.a`) available for C++ code (non-Rcpp) in other R packages (e.g. https://github.com/RGLab/flowWorkspace/issues/268) so that the same bundling and building efforts for tbb can be avoided? Currently only dynamic shared library (`libtbb.so`) is available but I guess it is not recommended to be used to link dynamically against the other package (see https://github.com/eddelbuettel/rprotobuf/issues/1#issuecomment-66241724) due to the potential runtime conflicts among multiple versions of libraries (e.g. tbb installed system-wise)

I saw https://github.com/jjallaire/TBB, which doesn't seem to be maintained recently, nor is it submitted to CRAN.

Should the type of the first argument be V*?

title: fix issue with PKG_CPPFLAGS
description:
From Professor Ripley:

> The following were unexpected: CPPFLAGS are for the C pre-processor (and 
> by extension the C++ one), not the C++ compiler.
>
> <...>
>
> RcppParallel/src/Makevars:PKG_CPPFLAGS += $(CXX11STD) -I../inst/include/
> 
> <...>
> 
> Most of these are compiler flags (as the Cxx in some of them hints), 
> including -g -O3 -std -W* .  And there is an official way to select 
> C++11: see 'Writing R Extensions'.
> 
> Please correct the package ASAP.

title: Remove link to BH
description:
Currently, `BH` is listed in the `LinkingTo` field of the `DESCRIPTION` file. As far as I can tell, it's not necessary.

It looks like `BH` was added in [this](https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/pull/20) PR (specifically, in [this](https://github.com/RcppCore/RcppParallel/pull/20/commits/a33642053e49e16afb99d49526cdcaafb463dcfd) commit), but it seems that `inst/include/boost` has since been removed.

I'd be happy to submit a PR for this, but wanted to open an issue first, since there may be some other reason(s) to keep a link to `BH` that I'm just not seeing. If that's not the case, let me know and I'll submit a PR.

title: GCC8 Issue: tbb/concurrent_hash_map.h:169:68: warning: 'void* memset
description:
Hi developers of RcppParallel,

I made a package via RcppParallel for threading. The input was CharacterVector, so I relied on TBB library.
I published the package [RcppMeCab](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RcppMeCab/index.html). However, the CRAN build test gave this warning:

```

I didn't use the concurrent_hash_map function in my package. But the current situation is similar to this thread: [GCC 8.1 warning](https://github.com/01org/tbb/issues/54). How can I solve this problem?

title: Setting and then resetting numThreads won't work
description:
Calling `setThreadOptions()` (i.e. with `numThreads = "auto"`) should call `Sys.unsetenv("RCPP_PARALLEL_NUM_THREADS")`, otherwise, the following happens:

```r
Sys.getenv("RCPP_PARALLEL_NUM_THREADS")
[1] ""
setThreadOptions(2)
Sys.getenv("RCPP_PARALLEL_NUM_THREADS")
[1] "2"
setThreadOptions()
Sys.getenv("RCPP_PARALLEL_NUM_THREADS")
[1] "2"
```

If the internal code always reads this variable, `"auto"` will not have the intended effect after reset.

title: CRAN comments re: C++11
description:
From Professor Ripley:

> Make macros containing CXX1X were replaced by CXX11 in R 3.4.0, but the CXX1X form has not yet been fully removed.
> 
> CRAN packages
> 
> RcppParallel icd9 odbc
> 
> still invoke them (in some cases for Windows only)
> 
> PWD RcppArmadillo RcppEigen cpgen perccal rENA
> 
> refer to them in commented code, and seqminer sets but does not use PKG_CXX1XFLAGS .
> 
> To avoid future confusion, please use the current form and remove unneeded references.  For packages which do end up using CXX11, please ensure that you declare
> 
> Depends: R(>= 3.4.0)

RcppParallel currently supports R >= 3.0.2, and I think we'd like to keep it that way. Hopefully there's an alternative way forward such that we can support C++11 on older releases of R in a CRAN-compliant way.

title: Package linking problem
description:
I have a preliminary package using RcppParallel, which is terrific. I was able to use "devtools::load_all()", but when I try to build the package with "R CMD build ..." I get a linker error. Not sure what I'm missing in the Makevars.

Can you try: devtools::install_github("harmonica", "thk686")?

Thanks.

title: resolve issue with `[[` use in Makevars
description:
The `Makevars` file makes use of `[[`, which is not available on the shell used with the new toolchain.

![rcppparallel](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/14406671/404ab04e-fe63-11e5-978a-a2665c8faa62.png)

Note the `[[: not found` lines near the bottom of the screenshot. Despite this, compilation does still succeed.

title: RcppParallel failing to install with the 4.9.3 toolchain
description: https://www.statistik.tu-dortmund.de/~ligges/3.3new/RcppParallel.Rcheck/00install.out has the output from Uwe's check. Seems to be a number of things which need to be changed in the Makevars. You should be able to check what version is being used by checking the `COMPILED_BY` make variable set to `gcc-4.9.3`.

title: helper classes for reading and writing vectors and matrixes
description:
VectorReader / VectorWriter

MatrixReader / MatrixWriter
- Provide iterators (begin/end)
- Provide operator[] for random access
- Parameterized on underlying type of vector (e.g. int, double)
